# Story 17 — Outbound email: send, thread preservation, acknowledgement, retry, log and test send (Story: 508)

## Prerequisites

- **Story 4.4 (work item #506) completed:** the `messages` table and outbound message creation path exist so there is a message to send. This story depends on `messages` rows carrying `delivery_state`, `subject`, `body`, `locale`, ticket linkage, and thread identifiers.
- Coordinate with **Story 5.2 (inbound correlation)** and **Story 5.3** owners: both depend on the exact `Message-ID`, `In-Reply-To` and `References` headers written here, plus the subject ticket-reference fallback. Do not change header shape without notifying them.
- Follow existing module-boundary rules in `backend/deptrac.yaml` and `backend/deptrac-tiers.yaml` — the Email module owns its own tables, jobs, and log; other modules interact through its **Contracts** only.
- Follow the settings-registry pattern established for **Platform Settings** (`backend/app/Modules/Platform/Support/Settings/*`) and re-used by the admin **SettingsController** (`backend/app/Modules/Platform/Http/Controllers/Admin/SettingsController.php`).
- Follow the admin section UX pattern from **`frontend/components/screens/admin/EmailSection.tsx`** and its parent `frontend/app/(admin)/admin/email/page.tsx`.

---

## Story Goal

Deliver the outbound half of the email channel end-to-end:

1. Agents' replies and system-generated acknowledgements on tickets are sent out as real emails using Laravel's mail layer via a configurable driver (SMTP, Postmark, Mailgun, SES) hidden behind a **MailTransport port** with a **null adapter** so CI passes with no provider.
2. Every outbound email sets `Message-ID`, `In-Reply-To`, and `References` from the thread; the ticket reference is embedded in the subject as a header-stripping-client fallback.
3. Sending happens on a **queued job with backoff**; terminal failure flips `messages.delivery_state` to `failed` and surfaces on the message in the conversation UI.
4. A new **`mail_log`** table (owned by the Email module) records every send attempt with direction, address, status, timing, and error; retention is a configurable setting.
5. An admin can send a **test email** from the admin Email section and see a clear success/failure with diagnostic detail, and can enable/disable/configure the channel and provider credentials write-only. Credentials render as "configured", never as a masked secret with reveal.
6. Outbound mail is localised to the customer's `preferred_locale`, defaulting to English.

**Out of scope:** inbound parsing/correlation (Story 5.2), SLA timers (Story 5.3), multi-mailbox configuration, WhatsApp/SMS/live-chat/web-form channels, integration console.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** the Email module has migrations for nothing; there is no outbound path; the admin Email section is a placeholder.
- **New behaviour:**
  - Outbound send is always via `MailTransport` port; concrete drivers: `smtp`, `postmark`, `mailgun`, `ses`, and `null` (default in CI).
  - `Message-ID` is set on **every** outbound message using domain from config `mail.thread_domain` (fall back to `mail.from.address` host).
  - `In-Reply-To` = the parent message's stored `message_id`; `References` = full ancestry (parent's `references` + parent's `message_id`, whitespace-separated).
  - Subject fallback: `"[#" + ticket.reference + "] " + subject` — do not duplicate if already present.
  - Delivery state transitions: `queued → sending → sent | failed`. `failed` is terminal after retries exhausted; UI shows it and offers **retry** (out of scope: manual retry UI is Story 5.3 unless trivial).
  - Retention: default 90 days; configurable; a nightly command prunes `mail_log` beyond retention (mirror `PruneIdempotencyKeysCommand.php`).
  - Credentials never leave the server: `GET /api/admin/settings` returns `"configured": true/false` for each credential; writing is `PUT`-only; audit-log every write via existing `AuditLogger`.

### 5 — Queued job + dispatcher

**Create files:**

- `backend/app/Modules/Email/Jobs/SendOutboundEmailJob.php`
  - `implements ShouldQueue`, uses `Queueable, InteractsWithQueue, SerializesModels`.
  - `public int $tries = 5;` `public array $backoff = [30, 120, 300, 900, 1800];` — reads from settings `email.retry.tries` / `email.retry.backoff` at construction via a small helper.
  - Constructor takes a `messageId` (string ULID of the message row). Fetch the message inside `handle()` to avoid stale serialisation.
  - Steps: reload message → transition state to `Sending` → build `OutboundEmail` (compute `Message-ID` if null, `In-Reply-To`, `References`, tagged subject, resolve `locale` from ticket contact → default English) → call `MailTransport::send` → on success: state=`Sent`, `delivered_at=now()`, write `mail_log` row → on `MailTransportException::retryable` → `release($this->backoff[$this->attempts()-1] ?? end)` → on non-retryable OR `failed_job` after last retry → state=`Failed`, `failed_at=now()`, `last_error` (sanitised), `mail_log` row with `status=failed`.
  - `failed(Throwable $e)` method finalises the `Failed` state so nothing is swallowed.

- `backend/app/Modules/Email/Infrastructure/QueueingOutboundMessageDispatcher.php` — implements `OutboundMessageDispatcher`. Marks `messages.delivery_state = Queued`, dispatches the job on the `emails` queue.

- `backend/app/Modules/Email/Infrastructure/AcknowledgementDispatcher.php` — implements `AcknowledgementDispatcher`. If setting `email.acknowledgement.enabled` is `false`, no-op. Otherwise renders template using customer locale and enqueues via `OutboundMessageDispatcher` after creating an outbound `messages` row of type `system_ack` (coordinate row schema with Story 4.4).

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Provider unreachable at boot (no config):** `MailTransportFactory` falls back to `NullMailTransport` and logs a warning once. Tickets still create and are assignable. Enforced in `MailTransportFactory::resolve()`.
- **Provider unreachable at send time:** `MailTransportException::retryable() === true` → job is `release()`d with backoff. `messages.delivery_state` stays `Queued`. After `$tries` exhausted, `failed()` sets `Failed` and writes a `mail_log` row.
- **Non-retryable send failure (400-class from provider, bad recipient):** state goes straight to `Failed`. UI badge surfaces error. Enforced in `SendOutboundEmailJob::handle()` around the `MailTransport::send` call.
- **Message-ID collision:** `messages.message_id` has a unique index. Job re-generates with a new ULID on collision (retry once inside job).
- **Missing `to` address:** validated in the outbound message factory before enqueue; job fails permanently with `error_code=INVALID_RECIPIENT`.
- **Unicode / RTL in subject:** subject is UTF-8, tagged with `[#REF-…]` prefix using ASCII brackets; `SubjectTagger::apply` is unicode-safe (uses `mb_*` functions).
- **Subject already tagged:** `SubjectTagger::apply` detects `/^\[#[A-Z0-9-]+\]/` and returns unchanged.
- **Very long `References` header:** truncate to last 20 ids (RFC-5322-friendly). Enforced in `ThreadHeaders`.
- **Locale not set on customer:** `AcknowledgementDispatcher` defaults to `en`. Setting `email.acknowledgement.enabled=false` short-circuits without writing a mail_log row.
- **Credential ever appears in logs or in a response:**
  - `JsonContextProcessor` (see `backend/app/Modules/Platform/Logging/JsonContextProcessor.php`) is already the entry point for log context — extend its redaction list with `password`, `api_key`, `smtp_password`.
  - `SettingsController` GET path must strip any setting with `SettingType::Secret`, returning `{ configured: bool }` only. Add a test.
- **Test-send rate abuse:** apply `throttle:6,1` middleware (per-user) to `POST /api/admin/email/test`. Also `IdempotencyKey` middleware for idempotent retries.
- **Half-applied migration (columns present but `mail_log` missing, or vice versa):** each migration is independent and reversible via `down()`. Boot does not fail if columns already exist (use `Schema::hasColumn` guards).
- **Queue worker not running:** enqueued jobs pile up; ticket creation is unaffected. Health check via a scheduled `queue:monitor` (out of scope) — documented in `backend/README.md`.
- **Concurrent state transitions:** wrap state changes in `DB::transaction` with row-level `lockForUpdate()` on the `messages` row inside `SendOutboundEmailJob::handle()`.
- **Custom headers stripped by transport:** `LaravelMailTransport` sets headers via the Symfony message callback which Laravel's SMTP+API drivers all honour — verify by reading Postmark/Mailgun/SES driver source at runtime and adding a test that asserts headers on the Symfony `Email` object.

## Migration / Rollback

- Migrations are additive and reversible:
  - `2026_09_02_000300_add_delivery_fields_to_messages_table.php` → `down()` drops each column with `Schema::hasColumn` guards.
  - `2026_09_02_000310_create_mail_log_table.php` → `down()` drops the table.
- **Half-applied state:** if columns are present but `mail_log` is missing, the job still runs but every attempt to write the log will fail loudly (caught in the job, re-thrown as retryable). Runbook: re-run `php artisan migrate`.
- **Rollback:** `php artisan migrate:rollback --step=2` restores the pre-story schema. Any queued `SendOutboundEmailJob` will fail on missing columns — clear the queue (`php artisan queue:flush`) before rolling back.
- **Feature flag:** with `email.channel.enabled=false` (the default) no outbound sends happen; the dispatcher becomes a no-op after logging a `mail_log` `deferred` row. This lets the code ship dark.
- **Credentials:** setting a new provider does not invalidate previously stored credentials in another provider group — clear them explicitly via `PUT` with an empty value.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend installs:** in `backend/`, run `composer install`.
2. **Backend migrates:** `php artisan migrate --seed`. Verify `messages` has the new columns and `mail_log` exists.
3. **Backend tests:** `php artisan test` — all suites green, including new `tests/Unit/Email` and `tests/Feature/Email`. `MAIL_MAILER=null` should be the default in `phpunit.xml`; if not, add it.
4. **Architecture tests:** `php artisan test --testsuite=Architecture`.
5. **OpenAPI:** `php artisan openapi:generate && php artisan openapi:check`.
6. **Frontend installs:** in `frontend/`, `pnpm install`.
7. **Frontend regenerates client:** `pnpm run api-client`.
8. **Frontend tests:** `pnpm test` — includes `messages-parity`, `openapi-drift`, `a11y`, component tests.
9. **Frontend lint / tokens:** `pnpm lint && pnpm run check-tokens`.
10. **Frontend runs:** `pnpm dev`; visit `/admin/email`; toggle channel on; save an SMTP config; hit "Send test" against Mailhog (or `null` provider); observe success card and — in Mailhog — a message with `Message-ID`, `In-Reply-To`, `References`, and `[#T-…]` subject prefix.
11. **Backend queue smoke:** `php artisan queue:work --queue=emails`; create a ticket reply through the API; observe the `SendOutboundEmailJob` running and the `messages.delivery_state` transitioning `queued → sent`; observe a `mail_log` row.
12. **Regression:** existing `tests/Feature/Platform/Admin/*`, `tests/Feature/Security/*`, and `tests/Feature/Tickets/*` still pass.

## Done Criteria

- [x] Agent reply on a ticket is delivered as an outbound email via `MailTransport` (verified in queue smoke + `HeadersRoundTripTest`).
- [x] Every outbound email sets `Message-ID`, `In-Reply-To`, and `References` derived from the stored thread; subject is tagged with `[#<reference>]` (verified in `HeadersRoundTripTest` and `SubjectTaggerTest`).
- [x] On ticket creation, an acknowledgement email is sent when `email.acknowledgement.enabled=true`, in the customer's `preferred_locale` (default English), carrying the ticket reference (verified in `AcknowledgementDispatcherTest`).
- [x] Outbound send is a queued job with backoff; retries are configurable; terminal failure sets `messages.delivery_state=failed` and never swallows the error (verified in `SendOutboundEmailJobTest`).
- [x] Failed messages surface in the conversation UI with an error badge and tooltip (verified in `MessageDeliveryBadge.test.tsx`).
- [x] `mail_log` records every attempt with direction, address, status, timing, and error; retention is configurable and pruned by a scheduled command (verified in `MailLogRetentionTest`).
- [x] Admin can send a test email from `/admin/email` and sees clear success or Problem+JSON diagnostic detail (verified in `EmailTestSendTest` and `EmailTestSend.test.tsx`).
- [x] Admin can enable, disable, and configure the email channel independent of existing tickets (verified manually + `EmailChannelStatusTest`).
- [x] Mail provider is chosen by setting `email.provider`; swapping providers requires no code change (verified in `NullTransportInCiTest` and by manual swap).
- [x] If the provider is unreachable, ticket creation and workability are unaffected; failures are queued, retried, and surfaced (verified in `SendOutboundEmailJobTest` retryable branch).
- [x] Credentials are write-only; `GET` endpoints return `{ configured: bool }` only; audit-log entry on write; never present in logs (verified in `CredentialsNeverLeakTest` and by extending `JsonContextProcessor` redaction).
- [x] `NullMailTransport` is the default in CI; full test suite passes with no provider reachable.
- [x] OpenAPI regenerated and drift test passes; message-parity test passes for new keys; a11y tests cover the new admin section.

> **Verified against the real mail layer, not only the null transport.**
> `RealTransportAssemblesTheMessageTest` sends through Laravel's `array`
> transport and reads the assembled MIME back. It exists because the rest of the
> suite missed a bug that would have failed every single send — see
> `.squad/gaps/17-508.md`.
>
> **Deviations from the plan, all deliberate:**
>
> **Credentials return `null`, not a mask.** The plan says `GET` returns
> `{ configured: bool }`; the registry previously returned `••••••••`. Both the
> mask and the value are gone: `value` is `null` for every secret and a separate
> `configured` boolean carries the only fact a reader needs. A mask is a
> value-shaped thing — it invites a reveal control, pastes into a config file as
> literal bullets, and on a screen share announces that something is there.
>
> **`messages` is `ticket_messages`.** The plan names a `messages` table; this
> repository has had `ticket_messages` since Story 4.1. Thread identifiers were
> added there as `email_message_id`, `email_in_reply_to`, `email_references`.
>
> **`customers.preferred_locale` did not exist.** The plan assumed it. Added as
> a nullable column in the Customers module rather than the Email module,
> because the preference belongs to the person: someone who writes in Arabic
> wants Arabic on the portal and in an SMS too.
>
> **A `TODO(Story 5.1)` stub was removed.** `POST /admin/email/test` was
> registered as a closure returning `202 {"status":"accepted"}`, and the admin
> console's button called it — so the control appeared to work while sending
> nothing. This story is 5.1; the stub is gone and the route reaches a
> controller that actually sends.
